estate_arrival.label: Padmini Amma's estate gate, courtyard and verandah
estate_arrival.anchor: Padmini Amma's Travancore estate: a tiled gatehouse in red laterite walls, a beaten-earth front courtyard with a great jackfruit tree at its edge, and the house behind with steep, low-swooping tiled roofs on dark timber posts over a raised front verandah reached by a short flight of stone steps. Small clay oil lamps burn in niches along the courtyard wall; the palanquins rest just inside the gate, where the Nair household guards in white, with swords and round shields, keep watch on the road.
estate_arrival.absent: No elephants, drums, heralds, banners or court procession; no fort walls, stone temple tower or European buildings; no chairs and no glass lanterns.
estate_arrival.time: dusk, the last light with road dust hanging in it, oil lamps newly lit in the wall niches

nalukettu.label: Nalukettu courtyard of Padmini Amma's house
nalukettu.anchor: The inner courtyard of Padmini Amma's house: a square of open sky above a sunken stone court, steep gabled tiled roofs swooping low on four sides with high latticed ventilation screens under the eaves, dark teak corner pillars carved with yalis and processions of elephants marching trunk to tail up the wood, and a black oxide floor polished to a dark mirror that holds the lamps' reflections. On one side an open doorway gives onto a dim storeroom of clay rice vessels taller than a man's waist; people sit on low wooden stools or on the floor.
nalukettu.absent: No chairs, benches, throne or European furniture, no glass lanterns or chimneys, and no stone temple tower or fort; the household guards stay at the gate, never inside the house.
nalukettu.time: evening deepening into night, clay and brass open-wick lamps reflected in the black floor

nalukettu_alone.label: The emptied nalukettu late at night
nalukettu_alone.anchor: The same nalukettu emptied at night: the sunken stone court under a square of dark sky, the black oxide floor holding the last reflections of the burned-down lamps, and a dark teak corner pillar carved with a procession of elephants climbing trunk to tail into the dark of the roof.
nalukettu_alone.absent: No other people, no chairs, glass lanterns or fort; nothing written or carved as lettering on the pillar.
nalukettu_alone.time: late night, the lamps burned low to their last glow

cellar_memory.label: The cellar thirty years earlier
cellar_memory.anchor: The same small earth-walled cellar thirty years earlier: low beams under the storeroom's plank floor with thin slits of light between the boards, straw-bound paddy bundles, clay grain jars, a woven mat and cobwebs.
cellar_memory.absent: No burlap sacks, no lamp inside the cellar, no blood, and no grown King, Prince or other figure from the present scene.
cellar_memory.time: near dark, thin slits of lamplight through the plank floor overhead, in a muted lamp-brown memory palette

storeroom_memory.label: The storeroom above the cellar thirty years earlier
storeroom_memory.anchor: The storeroom above the cellar thirty years earlier: a plank floor, clay rice vessels taller than a man's waist, a wooden post and one torch, with a doorway through to an inner room where a cloth cradle hangs from a beam.
storeroom_memory.absent: No blood, no firearms, no cup or buttermilk, no glass lantern, and no figure from the present scene.
storeroom_memory.time: night, one torch, in a muted lamp-brown memory palette

hunted_montage.label: Three slivers of the hunted boyhood
hunted_montage.anchor: Three narrow, separate slivers side by side: a bowl of rice pushed away untouched on a woven mat, small gold coins pressed into a palace guard's palm, and a figure with a drawn blade waiting on a moonlit Kerala road.
hunted_montage.absent: No single continuous scene across the slivers, no blood, no face of the King and no figure from the present scene.
hunted_montage.time: night: dim lamplight on the mat and the coins, moonlight on the road, all in a muted lamp-brown memory palette

verandah_rain.label: Front verandah of the estate in the rain
verandah_rain.anchor: The raised front verandah of Padmini Amma's estate house under deep, low tiled eaves, with carved timber pillars and dark doorways into the house behind, looking out over the wet front courtyard and its jackfruit tree. Rain pours off the eaves in sheets like a curtain between the verandah and the world.
verandah_rain.absent: No palanquins, guards or royal party, no Padmini, no chairs, benches or glass windows, and no umbrellas or European buildings.
verandah_rain.time: day, monsoon rain pouring in sheets off the eaves, grey wet light

storeroom.label: Storeroom off the nalukettu
storeroom.anchor: A dim storeroom off the nalukettu with a plank floor and rough walls, crowded with clay rice vessels taller than a man's waist. In its far corner a low wooden door that looks like nothing more than a repair panel opens on steps down to the cellar.
storeroom.absent: No burlap sacks, barrels, crates or shelves of foreign goods, and no glass lanterns.
storeroom.time: day, grey rain-light from the doorway behind

cellar.label: The hidden cellar under the storeroom
cellar.anchor: A small earth-walled cellar under the storeroom's plank floor: low timber beams, steps rising to a low wooden door, a woven mat on the earth floor, clay grain jars and straw-bound paddy bundles. Its only light is a small brass open-wick lamp set on the floor.
cellar.absent: No burlap sacks, barrels, bed or pillows, no glass lantern or candles, and no windows or daylight.
cellar.time: warm light from the single open-wick lamp, deep shadow beyond its reach

character_notes.nagoji: Thick curled moustache; clean-shaven chin and jaw, smooth skin, no beard, facial scar or forehead mark; long curly black hair with only the first grey at the temples. A tiny flush gold ear stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it; barefoot throughout this chapter, with no boots, talwar or silver chain.
character_notes.varma: Face, moustache and build from his sheet, with black hair, never the grey of the sheet's later figure. A private family visit: bare-headed with his hair in a side knot above the LEFT ear, no turban, crest, headband or crown, bare-chested in a cream mundu with a gold border and gold necklaces, and no spear.
character_notes.padmini: In her fifties with deep lines at the eyes and mouth and work-rough hands; thick black hair with a light threading of grey, coiled at the nape with fresh jasmine, and one simple gold chain. Her sari is worn in the old Kerala drape with no stitched blouse, her long walking stick in her hand or leaning beside her seat, and her face is never the Rani's.
character_notes.senior_rani: The King's sister, about his age, smooth-faced with a family likeness to him, taller than Padmini and very upright, cool and measured. Hair pulled back severely with NO flowers or jasmine, white sari with a narrow gold border and small gold ear ornaments; her face is never Padmini's.
character_notes.prince: About ten, with his uncle's sharp cheekbones and wide watchful eyes: a small clean white mundu, bare-chested, a thin gold chain and a small neat topknot. The same in every panel of this chapter.
character_notes.ramayyan: Thin sharp features and receding hair, plain unbordered white cloth, a palm-leaf bundle and stylus; no forehead marks or sacred thread. Never the officiating priest's face.
character_notes.revathi: A little younger than Nagoji: deep indigo sari with gold, braid looped with jasmine, a necklace of flat gold coins, gold armlets and a thin sandalwood line at the hairline. No tali, no red dot between the brows and no sindoor in the parting.
